subgoal_trace.result: The polynomial $x^n - 729$ is reducible over $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ if and only if there exists a proper divisor $d$ of $n$ such that $729$ is a perfect $d$-th power. Since $729 = 3^6$, this occurs precisely when $d \mid 6$ and $d \mid n$ with $d > 1$, i.e., when $\gcd(n, 6) > 1$.

subgoal_trace.title: 子目标2: Consider the special case when n is comp…
subgoal_trace.description: Consider the special case when n is composite vs prime, and use the fact that x^n - a^m factors when gcd(n,m) > 1.
subgoal_trace.result: The polynomial $x^n - 729$ factors non-trivially over $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ precisely when $\gcd(n, 6) > 1$. This occurs when $n$ is composite with a common factor with $6$ (i.e., $n$ is even or divisible by $3$), allowing factorization via the identity $x^n - a^m = (x^{n/d})^d - (a^{m/d})^d$ where $d = \gcd(n, 6) > 1$. For prime $n$, only $n=2$ or $n=3$ satisfy this condition, while primes $n \geq 5$ coprime to $6$ yield irreducible polynomials.

subgoal_trace.title: 子目标3: If gcd(n,6) > 1, then n is divisible by …
subgoal_trace.description: If gcd(n,6) > 1, then n is divisible by 2 or 3 (or both). Show that in these cases, x^n - 729 factors nontrivially.
subgoal_trace.result:
If $\gcd(n,6) > 1$, then $n$ is divisible by $2$ or $3$ (or both). In these cases, $x^n - 729$ factors nontrivially over $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ as follows:
- If $2 \mid n$, write $n = 2k$. Then $x^n - 729 = (x^k)^2 - 27^2 = (x^k - 27)(x^k + 27)$, where both factors are non-constant integer polynomials.
- If $3 \mid n$, write $n = 3k$. Then $x^n - 729 = (x^k)^3 - 9^3 = (x^k - 9)(x^{2k} + 9x^k + 81)$, where both factors are non-constant integer polynomials.
Thus, whenever $\gcd(n,6) > 1$, $x^n - 729$ is reducible over $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.
